result.title: Learning Implicit Solves for Dynamic Simulations
result.summary: High-fidelity simulation of dynamical systems is central to scientific discovery and engineering design, yet remains computationally demanding. Here we introduce the Implicit Neural Operator Solver (INOS), which learns the implicit solve and encodes a time integrator. INOS pretrains a neural operator from static equilibrium solutions and reuses it within Newmark-$β$ integration. At each time increment, the integrator forms an effective equilibrium problem, the pretrained neural operator infers the next-step solution field, and the Newmark relations advance the dynamic state. Numerical examples in linear and nonlinear elastodynamics demonstrate accurate full-field predictions without dynamic trajectory supervision. Comparative results show that INOS, evaluated zero-shot, achieves higher predictive accuracy than neural solver baselines trained on dynamic simulations. In addition, INOS delivers over 4,600$\times$ speedup in nonlinear simulations over sequential classical finite-element solvers. INOS natively accommodates changes in dynamic conditions and enables reuse of the pretrained operator across spatial and temporal discretizations. Further evaluation demonstrates a stable million-step rollout. These findings establish INOS as a reusable neural implicit solver for accurate, efficient, and robust dynamic modeling.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 INOS：先在静态平衡解上预训练神经算子，再把它作为 Newmark-β 时间积分每一步内层「有效平衡问题」的求解器，在没有动态轨迹监督的情况下预测全场响应，并展示零样本优于动态训练的基线、跨空间与时间离散化复用以及百万步稳定推演。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 VLM 推理无直接关系，但其「预训练算子充当内层隐式求解、外层固定积分格式推进状态」的混合结构，可能为 latent 循环中的求解式状态更新模块与长程稳定 rollout 的评价方式提供类比线索，可供核查。
